:::{#exm-differential-entropy-uniform}
#### Differential entropy of a uniform random variable

Let $X$ be uniformly distributed on the interval from $0$ to $a > 0$,
so that its [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf)
is $f(x) = 1/a$ for $0 < x < a$ and $0$ elsewhere.
Every value in the interval has
[surprisal](#def-surprisal-continuous) $\surprisalf{x} = -\log (1/a) = \log a$,
so the [differential entropy](#def-differential-entropy) is $\log a$ [@cover2006elements, Example 8.1.1]:

$$
\begin{aligned}
h(X)
&= -\int_0^a \frac{1}{a} \log \frac{1}{a} \, dx \\
&= \log a.
\end{aligned}
$$

With $a = 1/2$ and base-2 logarithms, $h(X) = -1$ [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit).
